story: On a breezy, clear Thursday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is heading off toward Town Square with a determined stride, while Donna, equally resolved, is checking the doubles ladder standings at the Rec Center. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal is content and making his way home, and Rosa, equally content, has just thanked him for the chair and asked him to come back around five-thirty to help set up the long table.
events: Donna (ladder standings board): Check where Pruitt-Kowalski stands on the doubles ladder

gary.thought_process: Rosa has settled Saturday dinner: Hal's bringing cornbread, Donna's got lemon bars, and I'm on ice and a six-pack. That's sorted and no one is waiting on me, so no need to chat more. Donna's already headed to the Rec Center, and I did promise her the match. My memory says I'm finally filing the Architectural Review paperwork today, which is the key to getting the cart lights and sound system approved under L-01. The right move is to stop chatting and go do something. Town Hall is in the town square, so heading there to file the review. That also lets Hal drop the matter. Then I can go meet Donna at the courts.

parameters.content: Heading to the town square to finally file the Architectural Review paperwork for the cart lights and sound system, then on to the courts to meet Donna.

donna.thought_process: I'm at the rec center with no one in sight, and Gary seems to be off thinking about where to go. Our doubles ladder match is coming up, and I already put Pruitt-Kowalski on the sign-up sheet. Best use of this hour is to check the ladder standings board so I know where we stand and what we need to climb.

parameters.content: Check where Pruitt-Kowalski stands on the doubles ladder

hal.thought_process: Saturday's settled: Rosa has my yes, Gary and Donna are in, and I'm bringing cornbread and the good chair. Rosa is right here and has her answer already, so no need to repeat myself. The paperwork is filed and the notices are posted, so my duty is done. Rosa's porch needs a seat, and the cornbread needs doing. Best use of an hour is to head home and get the chair and supplies sorted rather than stand around the street.

parameters.content: Heading home to see to the cornbread and the good chair for Saturday.

rosa.thought_process: Hal just confirmed Saturday at six with cornbread and his chair, and Donna is bringing lemon bars. Gary is the only one who hasn't committed to a dish, but I already told him to bring ice and a six-pack, and he swore to Donna he's coming. I shouldn't ask again or repeat myself. Hal is standing right here, so I can thank him warmly and give him something new to move things forward: ask if he'd mind arriving a bit early to help me set up the long table, which also builds the friendship I'm after.

parameters.content: Hal, you're a lifesaver, and I'll take that chair gladly. If you can come by around five-thirty, I could use a second pair of hands setting up the long table.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
